46e473a226b0e6d00fb7a5d80ceb89c4439cabc4.rationale: Higher score and presence of anti-centromere antibodies and Raynaud’s phenomenon, which are characteristic of Systemic Sclerosis

Systemic Sclerosis: F7: Vital signs are normal, which may not be expected in advanced Systemic Sclerosis
F8: Pulmonary function testing is within normal limits, which may not be consistent with significant pulmonary involvement in Systemic Sclerosis
F10: Tests for anti–Scl-70 are negative, which can be seen in some cases of Systemic Sclerosis but may also suggest another diagnosis
F2: Chief complaint includes polyarthritis and joint swelling, which can be associated with Systemic Sclerosis
F3: Previous diagnosis of idiopathic pulmonary hypertension, which is a complication of Systemic Sclerosis
F9: Laboratory studies show an antinuclear antibody titer of 1:320 and an anti-centromere antibody level of 94.8 AU/ml, which are often elevated in Systemic Sclerosis
F11: Examination reveals joint effusions, consistent with Systemic Sclerosis
F12: Raynaud’s phenomenon is a common symptom of Systemic Sclerosis
F13: Chest auscultation reveals coarse crackles, which can be seen in Systemic Sclerosis due to pulmonary involvement
